Sey morning addressed ambassadors, heads of diplomatic missions and representatives of international organizations based in Tehran, outlining the Islamic Republic of Iran’s positions on regional developments and providing a report on the diplomatic activities of the Iranian delegation attendied Abbas Araghchi, Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran, on Sundayng the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly. Referring to the Islamic Republic of Iran’s effective and assertive presence at the UN General Assembly, the Foreign Minister outlined the key activities carried out during his stay in New York, including consultations with the presidents and foreign ministers of more than 60 countries and senior officials of regional and international organizations, as well as talks with think tanks and media outlets. The Foreign Minister, stressing the Islamic Republic of Iran’s determination to safeguard Iran’s rights and national interests, provided explanations about Iran’s proposed initiative to restore security to the Strait of Hormuz within seven days, emphasizing that the world has clearly witnessed Iran’s continued goodwill and seriousness in using diplomacy to prevent an escalation of tensions. Araghchi added: “It became clear to everyone at this session that the Islamic Republic of Iran is serious about pursuing diplomacy, just as it is serious and determined in defending itself.” Elaborating on the Islamic Republic of Iran’s principled position regarding US excessive demands, the Foreign Minister stressed that if the adversaries once again choose the path of military confrontation and war, Iran’s response will be much stronger and more decisive than in the past. Araghchi also condemned the disgraceful conduct of US officials toward the delegation of the Islamic Republic of Iran, including the claim that members of the delegation had been expelled. He noted that the entry and departure of the Iranian delegation took place according to the previously announced schedule. Nevertheless, US officials, in an attempt to compensate for their failure to portray Iran as isolated, resorted to fabrications and claimed that the Iranian delegation had been expelled. He said this was, on the one hand, an overt admission of the United States’ violation of its international obligations as the host country of the United Nations and, on the other, an indication of US officials’ anger over the Islamic Republic of Iran’s effective presence at the most important international event. Elsewhere in his remarks, the Foreign Minister referred to meetings held with neighboring countries, including the Persian Gulf states, and stressed Iran’s decision to continue the process of building trust among regional countries based on the principle of good-neighborliness, with the aim of strengthening cooperation and coordination to promote regional peace and security. He also referred to meetings with European counterparts and stressed that the Islamic Republic of Iran had conveyed its positions to European foreign ministers on the need for European countries to adopt a responsible and independent approach toward issues concerning West Asia. Referring to repeated acknowledgments by NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte of the direct and extensive participation of European countries in the illegal and aggressive attacks by the United States and Israel against Iran, the Foreign Minister called on European countries to be held accountable for their role in planning and carrying out the US and Israeli regime’s military aggression against Iran. The Foreign Minister, condemning the inhumane and illegal US sanctions against Iran, stressed that sanctions, pressure and threats cannot undermine the Iranian nation’s determination to defend its rights and dignity.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Islamic Republic of Iran, condemning the illegal and inhumane actions and measures taken by the US government to disrupt Iran’s commercial exchanges and air transportation with other countries through the extraterritorial implementation of illegal US sanctions, stresses that these measures not only run counter to the fundamental principles of the Charter of the United Nations and international law, particularly the principle of respect for the national sovereignty of states, and violate fundamental human rights standards, but also constitute a dangerous plot aimed at undermining friendly relations among countries, particularly neighboring states. In this regard, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, recalling the deep historical, religious, cultural and people-to-people ties between the two nations of Iran and Iraq, and appreciating the fraternal relations and good-neighborly ties between the Islamic Republic of Iran and the Republic of Iraq, considers the imposed restrictions on civil air travel between Iran and Iraq to be contrary to the common interests and objectives of the two countries. Relations between Iran and Iraq go beyond the conventional relations between two neighboring countries and are founded on deep people-to-people ties and mutual interests in various fields. The travel of millions of Iranian and Iraqi citizens for economic and commercial activities, pilgrimage to holy sites, tourism, education, and medical treatment necessitates that issues related to transportation and communications between the two nations be managed independently, responsibly and with a forward-looking approach, based on their common interests. The restrictions imposed on air travel between the two countries, in addition to creating serious difficulties for hundreds of thousands of passengers, pilgrims, patients, students and economic actors from the two countries, are in clear contradiction with the nature of the strategic relations and good-neighborly ties between Iran and Iraq. While respecting the national sovereignty of the Republic of Iraq, the Islamic Republic of Iran calls for appropriate decisions to be taken in response to the US economic terrorism and sedition-mongering with a view to lifting the restrictions and restoring normal conditions for flights operated by the airlines of the two countries, in line with the interests and objectives of the two nations.

item.title: Iran urges Canada to answer for fate of indigenous children unmarked graves
item.description: Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Esmil Baghaei, in a post on X marking Canada’s National Day for Truth and Reconciliation, called on the Canadian government to provide evidence, transparency and accountability regarding the fate of Indigenous children and unmarked graves linked to the country’s residential school system. That question still haunts the conscience of the world when it comes to the Canada's Indigenous children who were taken from their families, stripped of their names, languages, cultures, and identities, and subjected to a system of forced assimilation. Many suffered abuse and neglect, and many died far from home and buried in unmarked graves. September 30 was Canada’s National Day for Truth and Reconciliation - apparently to honour residential school survivors and their families, and to remember the innocent Indigenous children who never came home. But reconciliation cannot be reduced to a commemorative day or political rhetoric. When serious questions remain unanswered and the history of residential schools is contested or obscured, reconciliation remains incomplete. The suffering of Indigenous children is not a culture war. It is a matter of historical truth and accountability. Questions surrounding unmarked graves deserve evidence, transparency, and an honest examination of the historical record - not denial, distortion, or silence. No reconciliation without truth. No justice without accountability.

item.title: Iran calls on France to respect human rights in handling protests
item.description: Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Esmail Baghaei, speaking to reporters, condemned the violent treatment of protesters by French security forces and called on those whose human rights claims have become deafening to respect fundamental human rights and basic freedoms when dealing with labor-related protests by school and university students. The Foreign Ministry spokesperson noted that French officials who describe the treatment of armed terrorists trained by the Israeli regime by Iranian security forces as a violation of human rights, themselves tolerate not the slightest violent act at peaceful gatherings against the police and suppress protesters in the harshest manner. At the same time, Baghaei stressed the need for protesters to refrain from violent behavior and causing damage to public and private property, as well as from attacking security and law enforcement personnel. Referring to reports published by French news agencies about the detention of more than 2,000 protesters and their being beaten by police, the Foreign Ministry spokesperson called for investigation into allegations that security forces had used severe violence against protesters.

item.title: Baghaei: Nihilism in US governance poses grave threat to human life and civilization
item.description: In a post on X, Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesman Esmail Baghaei warned that “structural nihilism” in the US system of governance poses a grave threat to human life and civilization, criticizing indifference to the consequences of military aggression against Iran. "In the end we all die anyway, so it doesn't matter." This is no conventional political statement; it echoes Albert Camus’s Caligula at the exact moment existential 'absurdity' curdles into tyranny - where the 'inevitability of death' is used to strip the living of their value. Because life ends, Caligula reasoned, the suffering of others is inconsequential. The terrifying difference today is leverage. Caligula had only the primitive tools of Rome; modern nihilism commands vast stockpiles of mass destruction. The greatest geopolitical danger is not a leader confronting mortality. It is a system that uses the inevitability of death to justify indifference to human suffering. “We all die” is a fact; “so it doesn't matter” is the leap where existential dread becomes a political weapon. Those who think they can appease Caligula forget that the absurd recognizes no rule or contract. Appeasement buys no safety - it merely negotiates the order of the victims.

item.title: Iranian Japanese Foreign Ministers hold phone conversation
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi and Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi held a phone conversation at noon on Thursday. During the phone conversation, the two sides exchanged views on Tehran-Tokyo bilateral relations as well as regional and international developments. The Iranian Foreign Minister elaborated on Iran’s positions and views regarding the situation in the region, stressing that the continued insecurity in the Strait of Hormuz and the Persian Gulf region is solely the result of the United States’ aggressive and interventionist actions, and that the only way to restore security is to stop the US’s illegal activities. Araghchi also explained the good offices by some mediators to advance the diplomatic process, stressing the Islamic Republic of Iran’s determination to defend its interests. The Japanese Foreign Minister, for his part, elaborated on Japan’s views regarding matters of common interest.

🔹Today is the last day of our stay in New York. We have had several very busy days in terms of the number of meetings that were held. We had a great many bilateral and multilateral meetings. 🔹The President, whom we had the honor of accompanying, had an intensive schedule, and I, too, had numerous meetings alongside him, both before and after his engagements. We spoke with the media and had extensive discussions with think tanks and members of the think tank community. We met with various countries' officials, as well as officials from the United Nations and other international organizations, and several objectives were pursued throughout all these engagements. 🔹First, it was to ensure that the voice of the Iranian people’s righteousness and their plight was heard by the world, to defend the interests of the Iranian people, and to demonstrate that Iran continues to be present on the international stage with strength and confidence. 🔹We encountered officials from many countries who were interested in engaging in dialogue with Iran, and a very large number of our meetings were held at the request of the other side. It was evident in these meetings that, contrary to what the United States and the Zionist regime tried to portray, the Islamic Republic is by no means isolated; rather, it is highly respected. 🔹It was stated in numerous meetings that both the people and officials of those countries genuinely appreciate what Iran did and the steadfastness it demonstrated in the face of what is ostensibly the world’s largest military. This steadfastness made many countries and many people proud. 🔹Another objective we pursued, which is a very important one, was to convey to the world the country’s positions regarding the war, and particularly regarding the Strait of Hormuz. 🔹There are conditions set by the Leader of the Islamic Revolution, and these conditions must be fulfilled for the Strait of Hormuz to be opened. Our mission was to convey these conditions both to the American side and to all other countries and the international community, so that they would be aware that Iran has a plan in this regard. Iran’s conditions are entirely fair and logical, and if the Americans claim that they are seeking an agreement or a peaceful solution, we present this solution to them. 🔹Our plan, which became known as the seven-point plan, was conveyed to the Americans through the Qatari intermediary. Despite the remarks made by the US president, I said that we were awaiting an official response from the United States through the intermediaries. Today, one of the Qatari intermediaries held another meeting with us. We discussed various issues and exchanged ideas on how to facilitate the fulfillment of Iran’s conditions and how these conditions could be met. They had some ideas, and we discussed them. They are going to raise this matter with the American side once again, and then the American side’s final response will be conveyed to us through the Qatari intermediary. They hope this will be done by tomorrow. 🔹I will fly to Tehran in a few hours, and whenever the Qataris have a response, they know themselves how they can convey it to us. These communications and messages exchanged between the Qatari and Pakistani mediators had already existed. Now, in light of the plan presented by Iran, they have taken on a more serious form. If there is a response, the Qataris will convey it, and a decision will then be made in Tehran based on that response. 🔹We have seen that, over the past few hours, a media campaign has emerged in various outlets, with claims being made and statements attributed to Iran. I categorically state that there has been no change whatsoever in Iran’s positions. Our conditions for reopening the Strait are clear. Our position on other issues is also clear. At present, there has been absolutely no discussion of any flexibility on our part.

🔹Our position is clear. At present, the only issue is the Strait of Hormuz. The reopening of the Strait of Hormuz is also contingent upon the fulfillment of a number of conditions that we have communicated to the other side. I would ask that no attention be paid to the speculation or deliberate media narratives being created by certain outlets.
